mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi Q7 30 TFSI / 55 TFSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the condition of the replacement unit and the specific engine code. Based on verified market estimates for V6 TFSI units, used engines typically range from £1,500 to £4,000, while reconditioned units cost between £3,500 and £6,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of HPFP or water pump failure in an Audi Q7 55 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Water pump and HPFP issues in the 55 TFSI often present as a gradual loss of coolant without obvious external leaks, or a check engine light indicating a lean running condition.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi Q7 55 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given that 4M generation models typically hold a market value of £15,000 to £45,000, a full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement is financially viable.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi Q7 55 TFSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straightforward supply and fit service for this variant typically takes between 3 to 5 working days, depending on the specialist's workload and the complexity of the quattro drivetrain and 48V MHEV calibration.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement engine affect my Audi Q7 quattro system or warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professionally installed, OEM-spec replacement engine with documented service history and a valid warranty will preserve your vehicle's resale value and quattro functionality.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi Q7 30 TFSI / 55 TFSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 55 TFSI badging on the Audi Q7 denotes the potent 3.0-litre V6 turbocharged petrol engine, introduced to replace the previous supercharged variants and offer a balance of performance and efficiency, often paired with mild-hybrid technology in later 4M models. (Note: "30 TFSI" is not a standard UK Audi Q7 engine designation; this page comprehensively covers the verified 55 TFSI 3.0L V6 powertrains that define this performance tier).

milestones.description: CGWA and CZDA engine codes introduced (3.0L V6 TFSI, 252hp) for the 4M generation, replacing the previous supercharged units with a more efficient twin-scroll turbo setup.

DZKA engine code introduced (3.0L V6 TFSI, 340hp) for the 55 TFSI badge, integrating a 48V mild-hybrid system (MHEV) for improved efficiency, smoother stop-start operation, and enhanced torque delivery.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi Q7 30 TFSI / 55 TFSI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Audi Q7 30 TFSI / 55 TFSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi Q7 30 TFSI / 55 TFSI is generally robust, but specific cooling and fuel system components carry known vulnerabilities. The CGWA and CZDA codes dominate earlier replacement demand for this variant due to HPFP and water pump weaknesses. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: High-Pressure Fuel Pump & Water Pump Failure
problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump & Water Pump Failure - Why the Audi Q7 30 TFSI / 55 TFSI Loses Coolant or Runs Lean
problems.affectedModels: Audi Q7 30 TFSI / 55 TFSI (CGWA, CZDA, DZKA, 2015-present)
problems.rootCause: Plastic impellers within the water pump degrade under sustained heat cycles, and HPFP internal seals wear, leading to coolant loss or lean running conditions that can cause severe internal damage if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of water pump, thermostat housing, and HPFP inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as preventative maintenance at 80k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded cooling and fuel components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if lean running or overheating has caused cylinder scoring or head damage

problems.recommendation: For the 55 TFSI, preventative replacement of the water pump and thermostat housing is highly advised before catastrophic failure occurs. If you are dealing with an earlier CGWA or CZDA unit that has suffered HPFP or timing chain failure, a rebuilt engine with the revised components is the most reliable long-term solution.

problems.group: Carbon Buildup & Timing Chain Tensioner Wear
problems.h4: Carbon Buildup & Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Audi Q7 30 TFSI / 55 TFSI Loses Performance
problems.rootCause: Direct injection lacks fuel washing over intake valves, causing restrictive carbon deposits. Early timing chain tensioners can also stretch, risking catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blasting for carbon removal and timing chain tensioner inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before secondary valve or piston damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt unit with revised timing components and cleaned ports, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain skip has caused secondary internal damage
